t: You're standing in front of the statue of John Wesley outside Wesley's Chapel on City Road. It was created in 1891 by the sculptor John Adams-Acton and is Grade II listed. The ten-foot granite pedestal beneath it was the work of Elijah Hoole, a Methodist architect. Wesley was an English cleric, theologian and evangelist, a principal leader of a revival movement within the Church of England known as Methodism. The societies he founded became the dominant form of the independent Methodist movement, which is why his statue stands outside this chapel.
